reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) from a single paper on a different HEA (CrNiFeCoMn) supports sigma/nitride formation at grain boundaries and associated property degradation in that system, but the hypothesis applies these findings to a different composition (Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3) without direct evidence, and the claim about behavior in both oxidizing and reducing environments is not specifically supported by the cited passages.
premises: Cr-rich sigma phase and nitride precipitates form at grain boundaries during elevated-temperature exposure in the HEA
These precipitates weaken intergranular cohesion and cause embrittlement
The as-built HEA is a supersaturated FCC solid solution with minimal secondary phases
Precipitate formation is diffusion-driven and occurs in both oxidizing and reducing environments
Aging at 950–1300 K increases precipitate volume fraction and reduces ductility/toughness
